title: Hotpath Explorer — probe flow and compact lanes notes
body:
Context and goal:

This is a working note for a compact, fast-to-scan "Hotpath Explorer" view in the Trace Viewer. Goal: help engineers rapidly identify the single most impactful path(s) for a trace (latency or error heat), compare the top two candidate paths, and then jump into span-level probes. Deliverable: wireframes + acceptance criteria + grooming backlog for a scoped MVP (no heavy instrumentation changes).

Key design ideas (high-level)
- Hotpath summary row: compute a single-line summary for each candidate hotpath (aggregated span names, total duration, suspect tag counts). Allows quick triage without expanding the full waterfall.
- Lane compaction: collapse low-importance spans into a condensed stripe (mini-bars) with approximate timings, while keeping key spans expanded. Users can toggle compaction per-lane or global keyboard shortcut (Cmd/Ctrl+K).
- Probe flow: from hotpath summary -> timeline preview -> span focus -> lightweight probe panel (quick-run metrics: avg latency, last 5 failures, sampled logs link). The probe should appear as a slide-over, not full modal, to keep context.
- Comparison mode: side-by-side mini-waterfalls of two hotpaths, with delta badges for duration and error rate. Clicking a delta opens a diffed list of spans (changed durations highlighted).

Wireframe notes (sketch-level)
- Top bar: Hotpath selector (dropdown shows top N candidate paths with % of trace latency), search, time window selector.
- Main pane split: left: compact list of hotpath rows (sortable by latency, errors, frequency). Right: detail canvas. Selecting a row drives the right canvas.
- Hotpath row contents: breadcrumb-like collapsed span chain (max 3 labels), total ms, error count, heat sparkline (last 24h), quick actions (pin, open probe, mark as investigated).
- Detail canvas states:
  * Timeline preview: condensed waterfall (no small spans shown), hover reveals tooltip with exact timestamps.
  * Expanded waterfall: classic waterfall for deep debugging.
  * Probe slide-over: three tabs — Metrics, Samples, Notes.

Micro-interactions and keyboard shortcuts
- Hover on compact stripe shows proportional height and latency percent.
- Double-click a hotpath row expands into full waterfall in-place.
- Shortcuts:
  * Cmd/Ctrl+1..5 to jump to top N hotpaths.
  * Cmd/Ctrl+P to open probe for selected hotpath.
  * Space toggles lane compaction.
- Animated transitions between compact and expanded lanes to preserve user's mental map. Avoid abrupt layout shifts that hide the vertical position.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
1) Product: When a trace loads, compute top 3 hotpaths from the trace graph (backend already returns candidate path IDs; UI must render them as rows).
2) UX: Hotpath rows show breadcrumb, total duration, error badge, and compact sparkline. Sorting and selection work without page reload.
3) Probe: Opening probe slide-over shows last 5 sampled logs (if any), simple latency histogram, and button to open full span list in the trace panel.
4) Accessibility: Hotpath rows are keyboard-focusable and ARIA-labeled; compact stripes have accessible text readouts.
5) Performance: Initial render of hotpath list + condensed preview must be <= 250ms on prod-simulated dataset (30ms token for API fetch excluded).

Open questions / areas for engineering input
- Backend: can we return pre-aggregated sparkline data for candidate hotpaths? If not, client-side approximation will be needed (costly on large traces).
- Coalescing logic: who owns thresholds for 'low-importance' spans? Product suggests configurable threshold (duration < 2ms or less than 1% of path).
- Caching: should pinned hotpaths be stored in user preferences? If so, need API/DB support.

Grooming backlog (rough tickets and sizing guesses)
- UX-1: Hotpath row component + list UI (1.5d)
- UX-2: Compact lane rendering + toggle (2d)
- ENG-1: API contract for top-N hotpaths and sparklines (2d backend + 1d frontend)
- ENG-2: Probe slide-over skeleton + samples pull (2d)
- QA-1: Accessibility and keyboard shortcut tests (1d)
- PERF-1: Optimize initial render (profiling + simple memoization) (2d)

Edge cases and constraints
- Very wide traces (thousands of spans): default to pre-compact mode and show message "Heavy trace: showing top N hotpaths". Provide link "Load full waterfall" which streams spans incrementally.
- Traces without structured logs: Probe should gracefully surface "no samples available" and present next-best info (e.g., recent error counts).
- Telemetry: emit events when user pins/probes/hides a hotpath for usage analysis. Track help clicks.

Notes from design review (2025-02-14)
- Priya: prefer a vertical mini-waterfall inside the hotpath row instead of breadcrumb; saves space but may be noisy. Try A/B with animated collapse.
- Ethan: additive delta badges with small color-safe palette. Avoid red for non-critical deltas.
- Omar: request rate-column would be useful for recent-failure-frequency based prioritization. Add if backend supports.

Prototype pointers
- Start with a static mock in Figma showing list + slide-over probe. Keep animations simple (fade+translate).
- Use existing waterfall component for expanded state. Implement compact stripe as a lightweight canvas draw to avoid DOM bloat for thousands of small spans.

Next steps
- Designer (Priya) to produce a 2-screen Figma mock (list view + probe slide-over) by 2025-02-21.
- Eng (Omar) to confirm API scope and return a sample response for top-N hotpaths by 2025-02-24.
- Product (Maya) to create the initial tickets in GH and link to this doc (will reference ENG-1427).

Misc scratch ideas (non-blocking)
- Drift indicator: show a small caret when a hotpath's shape changed significantly compared to previous runs.
- Telemetry-driven suggestions: "Investigate this path — 14% more latency than median" with one-click to open probe and a suggested guardrail.

Links and references
- related: Trace Viewer cadence notes (confluence) - linked above.
- Slack thread: #trace-ui -> ts: 2025-02-13 11:12 AM (discussion on compaction shortcuts).

Quick checklist for grooming session
- [ ] Confirm API response fields and example payload.
- [ ] Decide default N candidates (3 vs 5).
- [ ] Agree on compact threshold heuristics.
- [ ] Wire up simple telemetry events.

---
End of notes. This file is intentionally informal — meant as a collaborative sketch for the upcoming grooming meeting.
